projects.title: A11y Beast
projects.summary: A free accessibility checker. Give it a URL and it renders the page in a real browser, runs 110+ checks, and maps every issue to the 16 accessibility laws it could break, from the ADA to the European Accessibility Act.
details: Built with Next.js, TypeScript, axe-core and Puppeteer, plus 20 custom checks axe-core doesn't cover.
Runs on free-tier infrastructure, so it stays free and needs no sign-up.

media.caption: A real scan of example.com, recorded on 21 October 2026 and sped up 1.5×.
media.label: Screen recording: typing example.com into A11y Beast, running the scan, and scrolling through the report

projects.short: Paste a URL, get 110+ accessibility checks mapped to 16 laws.

projects.title: Nepal Tax Calculator
projects.summary: Works out take-home pay under Nepal's income tax rules for FY 2082/83 and 2083/84: SSF and CIT, the retirement-contribution cap, foreign income, freelancers and non-residents. In English and Nepali.
details: Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS and shadcn/ui, with the tax rules tested in Jest against real payslips.

media.caption: Recorded on 21 October 2026. You can also run the real calculator right here.
media.label: Screen recording: entering a monthly salary of 2,50,000 and then 4,00,000 rupees and watching the in-hand pay update

projects.short: Nepal's income tax rules as a bilingual take-home pay calculator.

projects.title: clairvoy
projects.summary: A command-line tool that reads your Claude Code sessions, shows where the tokens and money went, and writes CLAUDE.md rules that cut the waste.
details: Install it with npm install -g clairvoy. Below is output from its built-in demo, unedited apart from trimming.
projects.short: Shows where Claude Code's tokens go, then writes rules to cut the waste.

projects.title: AgencyHeight & customer portal
projects.summary: AgencyHeight is internal, so I can't show it. It's the Next.js marketplace about 3,000 insurance agents use, and I architected it from an empty repository: a Turborepo monorepo with 10+ shared packages for the UI, auth, API, state and analytics. Compared with the platform it replaced, it ships 30% less JavaScript and scores 46% better on Core Web Vitals.
details: I also led the customer portal in the screenshot. Policyholders use it to see their policies and ask for service, and it brings in 70 to 100 policy inquiries a week, about 20% of which turn into sales for the agents.

media.caption: The customer portal's sign-in and policy list.

projects.short: A marketplace 3,000+ agents use, plus the customer portal.
